title: Model profile release contract and pinning workflow
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and implement a single, auditable workflow for publishing Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) and an explicit version-pinning contract for customers and the runtime. This ticket covers: the API schema for published profiles, UI/Console publication flow, guardrails for verification and deprecation, the pinning semantics and API surface for customers, automation for profile verification and re-run, and observability/alerts for regressions after publish. Goal: reduce ambiguity about which profile a request uses, enable safe automatic rollouts between profile versions, and provide clear rollback and communication channels.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A profile publish API and Console flow exist that require a structured payload (model_id, model_version, profile_version, hardware_slice, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, throughput_tps, cost_per_token_estimate, verification_artifact_url).
2) Published profiles appear in the Verified Profiles catalog with immutable profile_version IDs and a visibility state (draft|published|deprecated).
3) Customers can pin to model_version or profile_version via API/Console; pinning to profile_version guarantees runtime will select that profile’s quantization/kv/batching config when available.
4) Canary rollout tooling can target a subset of traffic (10%, 30%, 100%) and will automatically revert on regression thresholds.
5) Automated verification runs (daily or on commit) re-measure core metrics and create a verification history.
6) Release notes and deprecation notices are surfaced in Console and via audit logs; all published profiles are logged in the customer audit trail.
7) End-to-end tests + integration test coverage in runtime and console exist and pass in CI.
plan:
Phase 1 (API + storage): design profile schema and enforcement rules; add DB model for published_profile (immutable id, metadata fields, verification status).
Phase 2 (Console UX): add 'Publish performance profile' flow with review checklist and required artifact links.
Phase 3 (Runtime integration): wire published_profile lookup path and pinning logic; ensure fallback rules when pinned profile not available.
Phase 4 (Automation & verification): schedule nightly verification runs and diffing tool; create rollback automation for large regressions.
Phase 5 (Docs + rollout): publish docs for customers and run internal training with support and SRE.
rollout_plan:
- Internal alpha: publish profiles for 3 internal models and pin an internal tenant. Monitor for 2 weeks.
- Beta customers: invite 6 customers to opt into profile pinning and canary rollouts.
- GA: open publish flow to all customers after 4 weeks of beta or earlier if metrics stable.
Canary thresholds: fail if p95 latency increases > 20% or error rate increases > 0.5% relative to baseline. Automatic revert on failure. Manual override available to SRE/product leads.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Create metrics in infra telemetry: profile_verification_pass_rate, profile_publish_rate, pinned_profile_miss_rate (runtime), profile_p95_ratio_vs_baseline.
Alerting: sev-warning when pinned_profile_miss_rate > 1% for 10m; sev-critical when p95 ratio > 1.2 for 5m.
Dashboards: Verified Profiles catalog, rolling verification diffs, pinned-customer latency breakdowns.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: customers pin to a profile that uses a kernel/hardware combo we cannot satisfy in their region. Mitigation: enforce compatibility matrix at publish time and expose 'region_coverage' on the profile.
Risk: Verification flakiness leading to false regressions. Mitigation: require 3 verification runs and median result; keep historical verification traces.
Risk: Overexposure of internal measurement artifacts. Mitigation: require signed artifact URL and redact sensitive fields in public-facing UI.
